question: A cement grinding laboratory reports increased hemihydrate after a mill ventilation change, but the plant suspects hot sample handling rather than actual gypsum dehydration. How should an engineering research agent separate in-mill sulfate phase conversion from post-sampling alteration before proposing process changes or buying a reference package?
category: Cement sulfate phase provenance and hot-sample handling
scenario: Apparent gypsum-to-hemihydrate shift following ventilation adjustment with uncertain sample cooling and storage
evidence_required: Time-stamped mill outlet temperature, ventilation conditions, gypsum feed chemistry and cement production lot
Paired immediately cooled and routinely handled split samples, sealed storage duration, ambient humidity and sample temperature history
Validated phase-specific laboratory method, repeatability controls and independent comparison of matched production lots
answer_and_decision_guide: Trace the exact production lot and collection-to-analysis interval. Compare controlled rapid-cooling splits against routine sample handling with an appropriate validated phase-identification method; assess whether the reported shift follows process conditions or storage history. Separate sulfate phase distribution from total SO3 and avoid diagnosing gypsum dehydration from a single bulk chemical result. Require plant engineering and laboratory approval before altering mill temperature or ventilation.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained engineering directory is a discovery source only; it does not validate sulfate phase testing. Use accredited laboratory methods and plant-specific process evidence.
free_first_decision: Use existing retained split samples, laboratory procedures and process historian records before seeking paid documents.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Check exact relevant file title, edition, method applicability, redistribution and user rights, current seller price, and obtain explicit buyer approval before any paid purchase; never purchase autonomously.

model_limitations: Without paired preservation-controlled samples and validated phase analysis, neither in-mill conversion nor sample artifact can be quantified reliably.
